{{nihongo|'''Hokki Shrine'''|法吉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
;Main deity: {{ill|Kisagaihime and Umugihime|Q11296639|qid=Q11296639|lt=Umukaihihime-no-Mikoto}} (うむかひひめのみこと)
;Associated deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508}}, {{ill|Futodama|it|Futodama|ja|フトダマ|ru|Футодама|simple|Futodama|zh|布刀玉命|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}
;Combined hall (Tsutsumi Shrine): {{ill|Omoikane|Q586088|qid=Q586088|lt=Omoikane-no-Mikoto}}
In the Hokki-go section of {{ill|Shimane district|Q11052337|qid=Q11052337}} in the ''{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}'', there is a tale that Umukaihihime-no-Mikoto transformed into the Hokki bird (hohokidori, i.e. the {{ill|Japanese bush warbler|Q27075456|qid=Q27075456}}), flew to this district, and enshrined herself there, and that is why the place came to be called Hokki. Umukaihihime-no-Mikoto is considered the same deity as Umugi-hime (clam-shell princess) who appears in {{ill|Myth of Ōkuninushi|Q11433656|qid=Q11433656}}.

Tsutsumi Shrine, which became part of the combined hall, was originally a shrine at Chisha-ga-ike in Hitsu-chō north of this shrine<ref>''Unyōshi'' records “Chisha Myōjin enshrines Omoikane-no-Mikoto” (Seki (2006), p.446).</ref>.

== History ==
“Hokki-sha,” a shrine with an official of the Jingikan listed in the Shimane District section of the ''Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki,'' is identified with “Hokki Shrine” in Shimane District of Izumo Province in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}.

A munafuda from {{ill|Keian|fa|کی‌آن|fr|Ère Keian|ja|慶安|ko|게이안|ru|Кэйан|simple|Keian|sr|Кеиан|sv|Keian|th|เคอัง|tr|Keian|zh|慶安 (日本)|qid=Q1146135}} 1 (1648) records the name “Ōmori Daimyōjin”<ref name="bunken1-2">Seki (2006), p.367</ref>. The 1717 gazetteer ''Unyōshi'' records it as “Ōmori Myōjin”<ref name="bunken1-2" />. In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 5 (1872), in March, it was ranked as {{ill|Q712534|lt=gōsha}}.

The former shrine site was northeast of the current site, behind the Uguisudai housing area<ref>''Unyōshi'' writes this place as “Uguisudani,” and the 1875 ''Kōkoku Chishi'' records it as “Uguisudani” (Seki (2006), pp.367-369).</ref>. Beside it is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|simple|Square Kofun|zh|方墳|qid=Q11504353}} said to be the “traditional tomb of Umukaihihime-no-Mikoto,” now maintained as a park<ref name="bunken1-2" />.
